narrative.title: The Conference Room Informant Scan
narrative.scenario: At a closed-door briefing, an informant is someone everyone else can identify but who can identify no one. Guests are seated in a grid where cell (i, j) states whether guest i can identify guest j. With at most one informant possible, a two-phase sweep eliminates guests pairwise until one candidate remains, then verifies the candidate against everyone.
narrative.inputFormat: An n x n binary matrix M where M[i][j] = 1 means person i knows person j.
narrative.outputFormat: Return the informant's index, or -1 if no informant exists.
constraints: M[i][i] is irrelevant (no self-knowledge is asked)
At most one informant can exist

testCases.explanation: Guests 0 and 2 both know guest 1, who knows nobody — person 1 is the informant.
Each guest knows the other, so neither can be the informant.

hintLevels: Level 1: Any single knowing relationship eliminates exactly one of the two people involved.
Level 2: Pairwise duels leave one candidate; the duel loser is whoever knows the other.
Level 3: The survivor still needs full verification — a candidate that skipped all duels can still be an impostor.
